facts: What a skill may be called. Narrow on purpose: a name holds no user prose, so a refusal may quote it back (see `invalidSkillsRefusal`) and a file written under it cannot escape its directory.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: project-settings
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+351/−44).

ai.title: Invalid skills refusal names the rejected skill and field
ai.summary: Adds `invalidSkillsRefusal` to `common/src/desktop-cloud/project-settings.ts`, replacing the previous generic 400 response for rejected cloud skill payloads with a specific message identifying the offending skill, field, and Zod error code. The implementation handles Zod v4 union failures by selecting the branch with the fewest issues, ensuring encoding errors in base64 uploads are not misattributed to missing fields in the plain upload variant. To prevent leaking user-authored content, the function only quotes the skill name if it matches the new `SKILL_NAME_PATTERN` regex, which was extracted from the schema to verify the name is safe to echo.
ai.evidence: The diff in `common/src/desktop-cloud/project-settings.ts` adds the exported function `invalidSkillsRefusal` and supporting private helpers (`reportableIssue`, `closestBranchIssue`, `renderIssuePath`, `skillNameAt`), and extracts the skill name regex into the new export `SKILL_NAME_PATTERN`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the Cloud route code that calls `invalidSkillsRefusal` to construct the HTTP 400 response, only the schema and message generation logic.

eli5.text: The rejection message you see when the assistant's cloud-based skill settings fail to save now names the specific skill and field that caused the problem. Previously, this error was a generic note that did not say which part of your setup was wrong, making it difficult to find and fix the issue. This is an internal improvement to error handling; no new features are added, and you do not need to change any of your own settings to benefit.

ai.title: Full access meter skips confirmation and applies solo discount
ai.summary: The Freebuff meter now supports a full-access policy where the server signals that no user confirmation is required for hour purchases or model switches via the new `spendWithoutAsking` flag. Additionally, a `soloDiscount` field is introduced to reduce the effective price of a session when no other account sessions are live, which the model meter uses to determine if a row is startable. This removes the wallet and session-ending confirmation prompts for eligible full-access users while keeping the list price visible in the UI.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `spendWithoutAsking` and `soloDiscount` fields to `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`. `common/src/util/freebuff-model-selection.ts` updates `freebucksRowIntent` to return 'allow' when `spendWithoutAsking` is true, and `common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts` modifies `getFreebuffModelMeter` to subtract `soloDiscount` from the price when calculating `canStart`. `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-chat-admission.ts` skips the confirmation phase for model switches when `spendWithoutAsking` is true.
ai.unknowns: The server-side conditions that trigger the `spendWithoutAsking` verdict are not visible in the client diff.

changes.what: Adds `spendWithoutAsking` and `soloDiscount` optional fields to the `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` interface.
Updates `freebucksRowIntent` to bypass confirmation logic when `spendWithoutAsking` is true.
Modifies `getFreebuffModelMeter` to calculate `canStart` using the price reduced by `soloDiscount`.
Adjusts the chat admission hook to skip the confirmation phase for model switches when the full-access policy is active.

eli5.text: For accounts that have full access to the assistant, the confirmation prompts that previously appeared before starting a session or switching models are now skipped. A new discount is also applied to the session price when you are the only person on your account using the service at that moment. This change affects users on full-access plans, allowing them to use the assistant without interruption and at a lower effective cost when working alone.

ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the implementation of the graphile jobs or the specific code changes in freebuff-web and freebuff-jobs that respond to this constant change.

ai.title: GitHub webhook receiver default switched from Convex proxy to Next
ai.summary: The `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_RECEIVER` constant in `common/src/constants/github-backend.ts` now defaults to `'next'` instead of `'convex_proxy'`, changing which handler answers `POST /github/webhook` at `/api/edge/github/webhook`. Under `'next'`, the Next route verifies the HMAC on the raw body and enqueues a single `freebuff-jobs` job for owned events, while forwarding other events raw to Convex. This flip is a reviewed one-line diff independent of `GITHUB_BACKEND`, allowing the webhook receiver to migrate to the Next route while background jobs still execute against Convex.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/github-backend.ts`, the default export `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_RECEIVER` is changed from `'convex_proxy'` to `'next'`, and the doc comment for `GitHubWebhookReceiverMode` removes the `(default)` label next to `convex_proxy`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which Next route file implements the `'next'` receiver or when it was deployed.

eli5.text: The service switched its internal default for handling updates from GitHub to a newer system that processes specific events directly before sending the rest to the old backend. This is an internal infrastructure change for the people who run the Freebuff service, so it does not affect anyone using the coding assistant or managing their own accounts. No one will notice a difference in daily use, and no action is needed from users.

ai.title: Add Purchase event to Meta Conversions API with milestone content name
